indicators.note: inside tells us the word for nail sits within the word for tooth

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel
a pin is a small nail

explanation.surface: Someone fighting tooth and nail to stand their ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tooth-and-nail' looks like the idiom for fierce effort, but it gives two separate pieces, and 'inside' puts the nail within the tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Coping means managing successfully, keeping up under pressure.

explanation.surface: An agreed payout taken from someone's purse.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement can be a binding agreement, and to purse the lips is to tighten or shrink them.

clue.text: Brush aside identical twin bears in the nursery

indicators.note: identical twin asks for the same piece to appear twice in a row

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the famous children's storybook bear

explanation.surface: Dismissing a matching pair of teddy bears in a child's bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss scornfully is to scoff at an idea as unworthy of attention.

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, nil
E, for east, is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A duck swimming in one part of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of north-east Africa.

clue.text: Standard sort of saint, adherent of a cause

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: sort of suggests a loose version, so the letters of saint are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conventional kind of saint who is devoted to some cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' is a golf-style norm here, not a flag; 'sort of' is the anagram signal working on saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a committed supporter of a party or movement.

parts.note: suggests a distillery underground, but means the pantomime lamp that summoned a genie in the cave of treasures

explanation.surface: A distiller working in a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, rubbing the lamp found in the cave produced a genie, a magic spirit.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to abut is to adjoin or border on

explanation.surface: A musician teaming up with a euphonium player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ABUT into the answer; the euphonium is a small tenor member of the same brass family, a fair if loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are deep-voiced valved brass instruments; the euphonium is often called a tenor tuba.

clue.text: Name it, in utter common sense

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation and the word it within the word for utter

parts.note: to utter is to say
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to name something while speaking plain common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete, but it is the verb, SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundness of mind and good judgement are what common sense amounts to.

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of saunas

explanation.surface: Money needed to build some new saunas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like funding for the saunas, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital city of the Bahamas.

explanation.surface: A fool who has got himself into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is slang for a fool, and noodles are a common ingredient floating in soup.

clue.text: Country doctor, not necessarily an orthopaedist?

definitions.text: Country doctor, not necessarily an orthopaedist?

parts.words: Country doctor, not necessarily an orthopaedist?
parts.note: a slang name for a rough-and-ready doctor that sounds as if it means a bone specialist, since it suggests cutting through skeletons

explanation.surface: A rural GP who is not a bone specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbones is an old slang word for a surgeon or doctor, from amputating limbs.

clue.text: Nevis Council, possibly, up in the air

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A local council on the Caribbean island of Nevis has not yet decided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the twelve letters of NEVIS COUNCIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unresolved and undecided is not settled by any conclusion.

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it signals sorting the letters of pier again

explanation.surface: A seaside town with an ideal pier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but means sort again, an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit at its peak of maturity is ready to eat, ideal for the purpose.

clue.text: A lyric poem that is terminal

parts.note: the indefinite article a takes the form an before a vowel
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Describing a poem that comes at the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' here is a noun: an electrical electrode.
explanation.definitionFit: An anode is the positive electrode, one of the terminals of a battery or cell.

clue.text: No end of ermine in the portico

indicators.note: No end of means the last letter of the animal's name is dropped

parts.note: an ermine is a stoat in its white winter coat

explanation.surface: Plenty of ermine fur on display in a colonnade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like the phrase meaning lots, but it removes the final T of STOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade in ancient Greek architecture.

clue.text: On the move, with a shake

parts.note: to stir is to move or shake slightly

explanation.surface: Moving about with a wobble.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion.

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
out means not allowed or not on, unacceptable

explanation.surface: Asking whether a turkey can be rejected for being fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the bird, but it is the country's code TR.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater game fish.

clue.text: Angry state of such long-distance runners?

parts.note: cross means angry
a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: The bad temper of tired marathon runners.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing over open fields rather than on a track is the kind of distance running described.

explanation.surface: Quitting a job because of some game.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm acceptance of delay or trouble is one sense; the other is the card game solitaire.

clue.text: Ten cents sent round in settlement

indicators.note: round places the word sent around the coin worth ten cents

parts.note: taken as written
a dime is the US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: Ten cents posted to someone as a financial settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' is what settles at the bottom of a liquid, not a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles to the bottom of a liquid.

clue.text: A sum etc, I call out, but get it wrong

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reading out a sum aloud and getting the arithmetic wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the twelve letters of A SUM ETC I CALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To miscalculate is to make an error in reckoning.

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud

indicators.note: a rendering is a version, so the letters of Verdi are reworked

explanation.surface: A passionate, loud performance of Verdi.
explanation.walkthrough: F for forte is a musical score marking; 'rendering' is the anagram signal working on the composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervid means intensely enthusiastic or ardent.

clue.text: Cowboy has a cough that is troublesome

indicators.note: troublesome suggests disturbance, so the letters of a cough are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ranch hand suffering from an annoying cough.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaucho is a South American horseman of the pampas.

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run the landlord

explanation.surface: A quick getaway from the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a hurried exit, but it means flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Élan is style and vigour, verve.

explanation.surface: A lively card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummy can describe something of or like rum, a spirit, and is also a card game of melding sets.

explanation.surface: A bird with completely black plumage.
explanation.walkthrough: The All Blacks are New Zealand's national rugby union team, whose players are nicknamed after the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Zealander, such as a player in the All Blacks rugby team, is nicknamed after the flightless national bird.

clue.text: Tasks for a patient chap on Sunday?

parts.note: Job of the Bible is proverbial for his patience

explanation.surface: Chores for a long-suffering man to do on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Jobs are pieces of work, duties to be done.

indicators.note: in puts the word for approved inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
OK means approved or acceptable

explanation.surface: A fuel that has been sanctioned for use in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is a solid fuel made by heating coal.

explanation.surface: A railway carriage waiting at the platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A victoria is a light horse-drawn carriage, and Victoria is a major London railway terminus.

parts.note: an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A British boxer in a light weight class named Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name, but it is the verb to bob up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to move up and down lightly, to spring back.

clue.text: Opening stride of a heavy round?

parts.note: a door is an opening into a building
a step is a single stride

explanation.surface: The first stride of a heavyweight boxer's round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is a round of bread: a very thick slice is called a doorstep in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstep is British slang for a thick slice or sandwich of bread.

indicators.note: in places the official's short title inside the word for a wager

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
a ref, short for referee, is like an umpire

explanation.surface: A penniless umpire who has been betting.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means deprived or lacking, left without anything.
